>
> And how can we test it?
> 
> I created a custom template and tried a 2D demo. I couldn't find any logs from `RemoteGodotFragment` or `GodotService`.

There two ways to test this PR:

- Stability test: the PR brings a lot of changes to `Godot.kt` in order to allow the `Godot` instance to be driven by a non-activity component. So the first set of tests should validate that no regression was introduced through those changes; i.e: existing use-cases and features should work as expected without bugs / regressions.
- Testing the capability itself: to test the new capability, you can use an editor build from the following branch - https://github.com/m4gr3d/godot/tree/implement_game_tab_using_service. The branch replaces the current embedded activity implementation with an embedded view that uses `RemoteGodotFragment` to populate its content.

I skimmed the code, and for the most part it seemed OK, although, it's a lot of changes and I don't think I spent enough time to really be comprehensive

I did a bunch of testing on the Meta Quest with [this branch](https://github.com/m4gr3d/godot/tree/implement_game_tab_using_service), which includes the changes in this PR (as well as a bunch of @m4gr3d's follow-ups), and didn't find any issues. I tested the XR editor, and running both a 2D and immersive project. I also tested using export templates built from that branch to deploy an immersive app to the headset. I tested using both OpenGL and Vulkan.

> * Use of vulkan + swappy causes `GodotService` to crash as swappy seems to require an `Activity` context

Since I only tested on the Meta Quest, the swappy issue didn't come up (it's disabled there), but this seems important to figure out for phones where it can make a big performance difference

> > * Use of vulkan + swappy causes `GodotService` to crash as swappy seems to require an `Activity` context

> By the way, are we sure about disabling Swappy? Just wondering if there’s a clear benefit to using Services that justify this change?

@syntaxerror247 The PR doesn't disable Swappy, I'll just add a note to the class `GodotService` documentation to mention that it's incompatible with Swappy at the moment. It's up to the user then to either ensure that they're using the class with OpenGL, or with their own build that disables Swappy.

The Swappy issue has been reported to Google, so I'll update the documentation for `GodotService` when they have a fix.

Edit: In the XR editor, Swappy is already disabled (as it doesn't support Quest devices), so there I'm making use of `GodotService` in order to implement the embedded Game window in my wip branch.

Yeah, I understand that this PR doesn't disable swappy. But choosing to use GodotServices ultimately means disabling swappy as it seems to be incompatible. 

@m4gr3d I think, using services should solve [this issue](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/103381). Have you tested it?

> Yeah, I understand that this PR doesn't disable swappy. But choosing to use GodotServices ultimately means disabling swappy as it seems to be incompatible.
> 

Yes, that's the price we pay for being on the bleeding edge :) 
I don't think the limitation will be there for long; I've highlighted to Google how they can address the issue, so we'll be waiting for their next feature update to see if the issue was resolved.

> @m4gr3d I think, using services should solve [this issue](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/103381). Have you tested it?

It may; one approach would be to switch the native engine to the service when the activity is stopped and there's a game running so the engine keeps being responding.. I'll investigate that approach after this PR is done.
